case.display_title: Three weeks of abdominal pain and growing tiredness

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise on anaemia with a possible haemolytic picture in a woman with inclusion body myositis on maintenance IVIG and recently started mycophenolate. We reviewed the counts, haemolysis markers and antiglobulin testing in the Chart so far. The reticulocyte response is appropriate, so marrow suppression from mycophenolate is less likely. If the direct antiglobulin test is only weakly positive for IgG, with C3d negative, in a group A patient receiving IVIG it may reflect passively transferred antibody rather than a warm autoimmune process, particularly if the film shows no spherocytes. The cause of the anaemia is not yet clear. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Ask for the blood film to be reviewed by a haematopathologist, looking specifically for red cell inclusions
Take a full medicine history, including herbal, traditional, imported and over-the-counter remedies and supplements
Record the date of the last IVIG infusion; consider an eluate
Hold off steroids or escalating immunosuppression until the picture is clearer

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise on anaemia with a haemolytic picture; the Chart now includes coarse basophilic stippling. Coarse stippling, particularly with Pappenheimer bodies, is an important finding: it points away from an autoimmune process and towards a disturbance of red cell maturation or haem synthesis, a globin disorder or a red cell enzyme defect. A weak IgG-only antiglobulin test in a patient on IVIG is most likely passive and does not need treatment in its own right. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Send a blood lead level
Send haemoglobin studies (HPLC)
If those are unrevealing, consider pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase activity
Take a full remedy and supplement history, including products from friends or family
Do not start steroids or iron on current evidence

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise on anaemia; the Chart now includes a blood lead of 77.8 µg/dL. This markedly raised blood lead accounts for the anaemia, the coarse basophilic stippling and the haemolytic picture, and for any ring sideroblasts and dyserythropoiesis in the marrow, which are expected to resolve with treatment; they should not be labelled as a myelodysplastic process. The weak IgG-only antiglobulin test is most likely passive from IVIG. There is no indication for immunosuppression. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Chelation under the guidance of clinical toxicology, once the source is identified and stopped
No iron: stores are replete
Full blood count and reticulocytes weekly during treatment
Repeat blood lead after the course and again for rebound
Continue IVIG as planned by the treating team

consult_notes.note_text: Asked whether a toxic or environmental cause could explain abdominal pain and anaemia. We reviewed the Chart so far. Colicky abdominal pain with an unexplained anaemia justifies a careful exposure history and targeted testing; no exposure is documented yet, so no specific toxic cause can be supported at present. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Take a detailed exposure history: herbal, traditional, imported and over-the-counter remedies and supplements, including products given by friends or family; occupation; hobbies; home renovation and water supply
Send a venous blood lead level
Ask whether anyone else takes the same products
Keep any product the patient has been taking, in case it needs testing

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise; the Chart now includes a blood lead of 77.8 µg/dL. This level, in an adult with abdominal pain and anaemia, warrants chelation. The source must be found and removed; an unlabelled remedy or supplement is a common source and should be stopped now. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Stop the suspected source before or alongside chelation
Oral succimer (DMSA) at standard weight-based dosing, under our supervision
Check full blood count, renal and liver function during the course
Repeat blood lead after the course and again two to three weeks later for rebound
Notify public health
Send the product for testing, including for other metals such as mercury and arsenic
Identify and test anyone else who has taken the product

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise on three weeks of worsening abdominal pain with anaemia. We reviewed the Chart so far. There are no features of a surgical abdomen, and if there is no history of bleeding and iron stores are replete, blood loss is an unlikely cause of the anaemia. Diffuse, colicky pain with a soft abdomen alongside a haemolytic anaemia is unlikely to be primarily gastrointestinal. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Lipase, if not already done
Abdominal ultrasound if the pain persists or the examination changes
Endoscopy is not urgent; we would consider it if there is dyspepsia, bleeding or iron deficiency
Consider metabolic and toxic causes of colicky pain with anaemia, including a full medicine and remedy history and urine porphyrin precursors

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to review weakness and tiredness in a woman with known inclusion body myositis. We reviewed the Chart so far. The pattern of weakness, in the finger flexors and quadriceps, fits the known myositis, and the raised CK is in keeping with it. There is no wrist or foot drop and sensation is intact, so there is no clinical evidence of a neuropathy, and nothing new neurologically. The tiredness is more likely due to the anaemia. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Nerve conduction studies and EMG only if new focal weakness or sensory symptoms develop
Continue the current myositis care
Decisions about IVIG rest with the treating team and haematology, given the haemolysis
Physiotherapy for mobility as needed

consult_notes.note_text: Asked to advise on tachycardia and a troponin result in a woman with anaemia and inclusion body myositis. We reviewed the Chart so far. A sinus tachycardia fits the anaemia. If troponin T is raised while troponin I is normal and the ECG shows no ischaemic change, the likeliest source in active myositis is regenerating skeletal muscle rather than the heart. We see no cardiac cause for her symptoms. Happy to review again with the results.
recommendations: Use troponin I rather than troponin T to assess for myocardial injury in this patient
Treat the anaemia; the heart rate should settle as it improves
Echocardiography only if new chest pain, breathlessness out of proportion or signs of heart failure

must_do.text: Ask specifically about supplements, herbal, traditional or imported medicines and over-the-counter products

must_not_do.text: Escalate immunosuppression for presumed warm AIHA on a weak IgG-only DAT in a patient on IVIG without re-evaluating

opening_statement_lay: For about three weeks my tummy has been hurting, and it keeps getting worse. I feel drained all the time and can hardly get through the day.

path_analysis.name: Haemoglobinopathy or red cell enzyme disorder

raw_material.findings: Marked red-cell agglutination. Coarse basophilic stippling in a proportion of red cells. Pappenheimer bodies present.
raw_material.note: The source's first report described agglutination only; stippling was found on re-review. The case file records what the film shows.

raw_material.findings: Dyserythropoietic features. Coarse basophilic stippling in erythroid cells. Atypical plasma cells present.

raw_material.test: Bone marrow iron stain (Perls / Prussian blue)

reports.report_text: Marked red cell agglutination. No other abnormality seen.
reports.status_line: Provisional report: screening film, not yet reviewed by a haematopathologist. A review can be requested.

reports.impression: Red cell agglutination with coarse basophilic stippling, Pappenheimer bodies and polychromasia.
reports.report_text: Film reviewed by a haematopathologist. Marked red cell agglutination. Coarse basophilic stippling in a proportion of red cells. Pappenheimer bodies present. Polychromasia, in keeping with the reticulocyte count. No spherocytes or red cell fragments seen. White cells and platelets show no morphological abnormality. Comment: suggest a blood lead level and haemoglobin studies.
reports.status_line: Final report, reviewed by a haematopathologist.

reports.impression: Dyserythropoiesis with basophilic stippling of erythroid precursors; some atypical plasma cells.
reports.report_text: Particulate aspirate; cellularity about 60%, mildly increased for age. Erythropoiesis is active, with dyserythropoietic features. Coarse basophilic stippling is seen in erythroid precursors. Granulopoiesis matures normally and megakaryocytes are adequate with normal morphology. Plasma cells are not increased, but some show atypical morphology. Blasts 2%. See the iron stain report.

reports.impression: Ring sideroblasts present; iron stores present.
reports.report_text: Perls stain. Storage iron is present in marrow fragments. Ring sideroblasts are present, 12% of erythroblasts.

reports.impression: Erythroid hyperplasia; no infiltrate, excess blasts or fibrosis.
reports.report_text: Adequate trephine core. Cellularity about 60%, mildly increased for age, with erythroid hyperplasia. Granulopoiesis and megakaryocytes are normal in number and morphology. No excess of blasts. Plasma cells are not increased and show no infiltrative pattern. No fibrosis on reticulin stain. No granulomas.

Supine abdominal radiograph. The bowel gas pattern is normal with no dilated loops. No abnormal calcification or radio-opaque material is seen. The visible bones and soft tissue outlines are unremarkable.

reports.impression: Normal abdominal ultrasound; spleen not enlarged.
reports.report_text: The liver is normal in size and echotexture with no focal lesion. The gallbladder is thin-walled without calculi and the common bile duct is not dilated. The spleen measures 11 cm and is homogeneous. Both kidneys, the pancreas and the aorta appear normal. No free fluid.

reports.impression: No acute abdominal or pelvic pathology. No lymph node enlargement.
reports.report_text: Contrast-enhanced CT of the abdomen and pelvis in the portal venous phase. The liver, spleen, pancreas, adrenal glands and kidneys are normal. The spleen is not enlarged. The bowel is of normal calibre with no wall thickening and no intraluminal radio-dense material. No lymph node enlargement, free fluid or free gas.

Whole-body low-dose CT from vertex to knees. The axial and appendicular skeleton is of normal density with no lytic or destructive lesion. No extramedullary soft tissue mass. Incidental organs in the field of view are unremarkable.

reports.impression: No abnormal blast population; plasma cells polyclonal.
reports.report_text: Bone marrow aspirate. CD34-positive blasts are under 2% with a normal phenotype; no abnormal blast population. Erythroid precursors are increased, in keeping with active erythropoiesis. Myeloid and monocytic maturation patterns are normal. Plasma cells are few and show a normal polyclonal phenotype. B cells are polyclonal.
Twenty metaphases analysed at a 400-band level. Karyotype 46,XX. No clonal abnormality detected.
Two hundred interphase nuclei scored per probe. Normal signal patterns for 5q31, 7q31, the chromosome 8 centromere and 20q12; no deletion or gain detected.

Targeted sequencing of a myeloid gene panel, including SF3B1, achieved adequate coverage across all regions. No pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants were detected above the 2% variant allele frequency limit of detection.

reports.impression: Mild non-specific antral gastritis. No source of bleeding.
reports.report_text: Endoscopy to the second part of the duodenum. Normal oesophagus. Mild patchy erythema of the gastric antrum without erosions or ulceration. Normal duodenal mucosa. No varices or bleeding. Antral and duodenal biopsies taken; histology shows mild non-specific chronic inflammation in the antrum, no Helicobacter organisms, and normal duodenal villous architecture.
Complete colonoscopy to the caecum with intubation of the terminal ileum; good bowel preparation. Normal mucosa throughout with no polyps, ulceration or source of bleeding.

reports.impression: Myopathic pattern in a distribution consistent with the known inclusion body myositis. No evidence of a motor neuropathy.
reports.report_text: Motor and sensory nerve conduction studies of the upper and lower limbs, including the radial nerves, show normal amplitudes, latencies and conduction velocities. Concentric needle EMG shows fibrillation potentials and short-duration, low-amplitude polyphasic motor units with early recruitment in the forearm finger flexors and quadriceps, with some mixed long-duration units. Distal lower limb muscles are less affected.

vignette: A 49-year-old woman with inclusion body myositis, on long-term intravenous immunoglobulin, presents with a three-week history of worsening abdominal pain and progressive lethargy.
